summary: The American Clean Power Association and Southern Renewable Energy Association protest MISO's LARS filing as unduly discriminatory against independent power producers, a permanent uncapped expedited queue, and unlike the service described in the show cause order. They ask FERC to reject it or clarify the same-LRZ test.
ask: Reject LARS; if any part is accepted, direct MISO to clarify that the same-LRZ test turns on the point of interconnection, not the generator's physical location.

points.point: The trades say LARS goes further than ERAS: permanent, uncapped, untethered to a resource adequacy need, and run through the load-serving entity.
points.quote: It is permanent and uncapped. It is untethered to any identified resource adequacy need.

points.point: They say making the LSE the applicant gives LSEs gatekeeper control over a jurisdictional interconnection process.
points.quote: LARS is unduly discriminatory because it makes the LSE the gatekeeper of a Commission-jurisdictional generator interconnection process

points.point: They contend the show cause order did not call for a permanent expedited queue and described interim service until ERIS or NRIS.
points.quote: The Show Cause Order did not direct MISO to create a separate, permanent, expedited generator interconnection queue.

points.point: They cite bounded precedents: PJM RRI at 50 projects and MISO ERAS at 68 requests ending by August 31, 2027.
points.quote: The revised MISO ERAS process is capped at 68 requests and sunsets no later than August 31, 2027

points.point: They argue same-LRZ pairing grants broad injection rights to generators that need not be operationally tied to the load.
points.quote: its same-LRZ pairing grants broad priority injection rights to generators that need not be operationally tied to the load.

points.point: They note LARS studies exclude DPP requests lacking executed GIAs, which they say shifts capacity and costs away from DPP customers.
points.quote: exclude DPP Interconnection Requests that lack an executed Generator Interconnection

points.point: They say MISO has not shown LARS meets the independent entity variation standard.
points.quote: MISO has not shown that LARS satisfies the independent entity variation standard.

points.point: As a fallback, they request clarification that the same-LRZ test uses the point of interconnection.
points.quote: the relevant location is the applicable POI to the MISO Transmission System rather than the physical location of the Generating Facility

throughLine.text: Protests MISO's LARS filing as a departure from the interim, output-limited service for electrically proximate large loads that the E-8 show cause order described.
